Synthetic note for software demonstration only; no real patient.
Patient: Marian Delacroix. MRN: 00481516. Date of birth: 03/14/1957.
Procedure date: 02/11/2026.

Indication: 22 mm solid nodule in the posterior segment of the right upper lobe with enlarged right paratracheal and subcarinal lymph nodes on CT. Diagnosis and mediastinal staging.
Procedures performed: robotic bronchoscopy and linear EBUS-TBNA. Both procedures were completed.
Anesthesia: general anesthesia with an 8.5 mm endotracheal tube. ASA class III.

Linear EBUS: A systematic mediastinal and hilar survey was performed. Station 4R was sampled. The station 4R node measured 12 mm in short axis on ultrasound, and three passes were made with a 22-gauge needle. Station 7 was sampled. The station 7 node measured 14 mm in short axis on ultrasound, and four passes were made with a 22-gauge needle. Station 11L was surveyed and measured 4 mm in short axis on ultrasound. Station 11L was not sampled because it was small with benign sonographic features. ROSE showed lymphocytes at station 4R and at station 7. The station 4R material was sent as specimen C for cytology. The station 7 material was sent as specimen D for cytology.

Robotic bronchoscopy: The Ion platform was used to navigate to target T1, the 22 mm solid nodule in the posterior segment of the right upper lobe. A bronchus sign was present on CT. Navigation to T1 was successful. Radial EBUS showed an eccentric view. Cone-beam CT confirmed the needle within the lesion. T1 was sampled with a 21-gauge needle for four passes. T1 was then sampled with forceps for five biopsies. ROSE of the needle passes from T1 showed atypical cells. The needle material from T1 was sent as specimen A for cytology. The forceps biopsies from T1 were sent as specimen B for histology.

Complications: none. There was no pneumothorax on post-procedure fluoroscopy. The patient was extubated and discharged home after recovery.
samples.title: Combined case: lung nodule biopsy, 4R and 7 sampled, 11L surveyed

SYNTHETIC REGISTRY DEMO REBUS-20181221-01
FICTIONAL SANDBOX DATA ONLY. This note was created for software testing and is not a record of care.
Patient: Henry Clin Doc (Epic synthetic patient). Age at procedure: 68 years. Sex: male.
Procedure date: 2018-12-21.
Indication: diagnostic evaluation of an 18 mm solid right upper lobe lung nodule and mediastinal staging.
Planned and performed: diagnostic robotic bronchoscopy and linear EBUS-TBNA. Both procedures were completed.
General anesthesia; ASA III; oral endotracheal tube 8.5 mm. Procedure duration 65 minutes.
Robotic bronchoscopy: The Monarch platform was used to navigate to prespecified target T1, an 18 mm solid lesion in the posterior segment of the right upper lobe. CT bronchus sign was present. Navigation to T1 was successful. Radial EBUS showed a concentric pattern. Mobile cone-beam CT then confirmed the biopsy needle within the lesion. No repositioning was required after confirmation.
Sampling T1: A 21-gauge needle was used for four passes in total. These are aggregate acquisition counts; individual pass records were not documented. All material was submitted as specimen A, right upper lobe target T1. ROSE showed atypical cells; adequacy was indeterminate. Final pathology was pending at the end of the procedure.
Linear EBUS: The mediastinum was surveyed for staging. Station 7 was visualized and sampled. A station 7 node measured 10 mm in ultrasound short axis. Three passes were performed with a 22-gauge needle and submitted as specimen B, station 7. ROSE showed lymphocytes and was adequate. Station 4R was visualized but not sampled because an intervening vessel prevented a safe needle path. No short-axis measurement was documented for 4R.
Immediate complications: none observed. No complication treatment was required. The patient was extubated and discharged home after recovery.
Follow-up: 0-7 day and 8-30 day safety outcomes were not yet assessed. Final diagnosis and molecular adequacy were pending.

Robotic Bronchoscopy Procedure Report
Procedure date: 2026-01-17

INDICATION
The patient is a 64-year-old male, current smoker (10 pack-years). Indication: tissue diagnosis of a peripheral lung lesion and mediastinal staging.

ANESTHESIA
Moderate sedation was used with a natural airway.

PROCEDURES
Robotic-assisted bronchoscopy was performed as planned and completed. Linear EBUS-TBNA was performed as planned and completed.

ROBOTIC NAVIGATION AND SAMPLING
The Monarch robotic platform was used for navigation. Target 1 was a 38 mm solid lesion in the lingula. A bronchus sign was present. The robotic catheter was navigated to target 1, and the target was reached and sampled. Radial EBUS showed an eccentric view. Transbronchial forceps biopsies were obtained. ROSE of target 1 showed scant cellularity, nondiagnostic; the sample was not adequate. Specimen A: forceps biopsies from target 1 (histology).

LINEAR EBUS
Linear EBUS was performed for initial mediastinal staging using a systematic sampling strategy. The systematic nodal examination was complete. Station 10R was visualized on EBUS and sampled. Station 10R: EBUS-guided TBNA with a 25-gauge needle, 2 passes. Specimen B: station 10R aspirates (cytology). Station 11R was visualized on EBUS but not sampled because it appeared benign on ultrasound. Station 2R was visualized on EBUS but not sampled because it appeared benign on ultrasound. Station 2R measured 3 mm in short axis. Station 10L was visualized on EBUS but not sampled because it appeared benign on ultrasound. Station 4L was visualized on EBUS but not sampled because it measured under 5 mm with benign sonographic features. Station 4R was visualized on EBUS but not sampled because it appeared benign on ultrasound. Station 4R measured 8 mm in short axis.

COMPLICATIONS
A small left pneumothorax occurred immediately after the robotic biopsies and was managed with observation and no pleural intervention.
